text:
### Observed differences

- The relative order of the pair A26/A27 and the group A35/A36/A41 reversed. In the earlier window, A26 ran before A35, A36 and A41 in about 98–99 in 100 traces, and A27 ran before them in at least about 98 in 100; in the later window, both A26 and A27 ran after the group in about 97–98 in 100 traces. All six activities still occurred together in essentially every trace in both windows (co-occurrence 100%, 200 of 200 traces in each window). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- Successor relations changed accordingly. In the earlier window, about 98 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions went to A27; in the later window they spread almost evenly over A35, A36 and A41 (about 31–33% each, together about 97%). A26's outgoing transitions, previously split about 38% to A41, 33% to A35 and 28% to A36, went in the later window about 98 in 100 to A30. Each of A35, A36 and A41 sent roughly a third of its outgoing transitions to A30 in the earlier window (28–38%); in the later window these A30 edges were observed only rarely (about 1 in 200) and each sent about 27–35% to A27 instead. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- Event positions shifted consistently with the reversal: A26's mean relative position moved from about 0.53 to about 0.62 of the trace and A27's from about 0.38 to about 0.47, while A35, A36 and A41 moved earlier, from about 0.58–0.59 to about 0.42 (positions are event ranks within the case, not clock times). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering in which the segment containing A26 and A27, which previously executed before the group A35/A36/A41, now executes after it. In the earlier window the flow ran from A25 to A27, then through A26 into the group A35/A36/A41, which led on to A30; in the later window A25 leads into the group A35/A36/A41, the group leads to A27, and A26 leads to A30, while the internal order within the pair (A27 earlier) and within the group appears unchanged. Supporting signs: the order reversal is observed directly and is near-deterministic within each window (about 98–100 in 100 one way before, about 97–98 in 100 the other way after); the successor changes are coordinated across all five analysed source activities; the position shifts agree in direction and size; participation is unchanged (co-occurrence 100% and 200 of 200 traces in both windows); and the 16 qualifying control-flow items are roughly 30 times the 0.53 expected by chance across 106 units, so chance sampling cannot account for the set as a whole. The DIR, POS and REL items largely reflect this one underlying reordering rather than independent confirmations of it. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: A27's outgoing transitions and the group's incoming edges were not analysed, so the new wiring between A27 and A26 (for example whether A27 now precedes A26) is inferred from event positions rather than observed directly; and the evidence cannot distinguish a rewiring of a single flow from a change in which of two fixed process variants dominates, although the near-deterministic order within each window makes a shift in the mix of orders unlikely. [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Other differences: only noise-level changes — rare outgoing transitions (about 1 in 200) appear or disappear in the successor profiles, and the interleaving of A27 with the group rises slightly from about 1 to about 2 in 100 traces. [DIR001, DIR002, REL004, REL005, REL006]
